deployment_assumptions: Once deployed, MOSFETs are not typically replaceable or updatable. Devices may be physically accessible to attackers and are expected to have a long operational life without intervention.
open_questions: What specific use cases or environmental conditions are anticipated for these MOSFETs?
What measures are currently in place for gate oxide quality control during manufacturing?
Can more detailed asset-specific clarity (e.g., key type, authorization model) be provided?
prioritization_summary: Security prioritization focuses on threats to cryptographic keys and authorization states directly impacted by electrical properties and degradation risks as they relate to MOSFET terminals and channels.

prioritized_actions.next_step: Conduct detailed leakage path simulations for known cryptographic current states.
prioritized_actions.rationale: Immediate leakage risks to cryptographic elements must be prioritized due to their critical impact and lack of mitigation post-release.
prioritized_actions.title: Sub-threshold Leakage Exploit

prioritized_actions.next_step: Integrate leakage mitigation strategies into design, focusing on known vulnerable states.
prioritized_actions.rationale: Simultaneous with understanding leakage paths, robust leakage controls should be integrated into design to avoid confidentiality breaches.
prioritized_actions.title: Sub-threshold Leakage Mitigation

prioritized_actions.next_step: Verify oxide resistance with stress tests applied to a pre-production batch.
prioritized_actions.rationale: Gate reliability impacts device operation longevity and security; must be addressed pre-fabrication.
prioritized_actions.title: Gate Oxide Breakdown

prioritized_actions.next_step: Allocate manufacturing QA resources to implement rigorous oxide testing.
prioritized_actions.rationale: Ensuring oxide integrity through stress and environmental testing is vital for long-term device reliability.
prioritized_actions.title: Gate Oxide Integrity Assurance

prioritized_actions.next_step: Review signal amplification safeguards for compliance with design constraints.
prioritized_actions.rationale: Direct interface threats highlight need for strict signal control to maintain circuit integrity and security post-deployment.
prioritized_actions.title: Unauthorized Signal Amplification

security_requirements.description: Ensure leakage paths are minimized to protect against cryptographic key inference.
security_requirements.design_robustness: Leakage control designed into MOSFETs remains effective despite deployment environment.
security_requirements.priority_rationale: Early detection and prevention of leakage paths must be prioritized to protect sensitive assets.
security_requirements.requirement: The design shall minimize sub-threshold leakage currents below detectable limits for all cryptographic operations.
security_requirements.title: Sub-threshold Leakage Mitigation
security_requirements.verification_method: Simulate and measure leakage currents under worst-case operating conditions during design validation.

security_requirements.description: Manufacturing processes shall ensure robust gate oxide layers resistant to breakdown.
security_requirements.design_robustness: Ensures long-term device reliability despite stress or aging, unalterable post-fabrication.
security_requirements.priority_rationale: Manufacturing constraints must ensure resilience of the oxide layer to prevent future failures.
security_requirements.requirement: The manufacturing process shall produce gate oxides that withstand stress conditions exceeding operational specifications without degradation.
security_requirements.title: Gate Oxide Integrity Assurance
security_requirements.verification_method: Environmental and stress testing of representative devices in pre-production batches.

security_requirements.description: Design must prevent unauthorized signal amplification through MOSFETs.
security_requirements.design_robustness: Implemented amplification restraints are intrinsic to design; durable post-deployment.
security_requirements.priority_rationale: Preempting signal control issues is critical to protect system operational integrity.
security_requirements.requirement: The MOSFET design should include measures that prevent signal amplification beyond control parameters, addressing both intentional and unintentional misuse.
security_requirements.title: Controlled Signal Amplification
security_requirements.verification_method: Perform circuit analysis and testing to validate signal amplification controls under varied conditions.

summary: MOSFETs are fundamental to digital circuit operations and security at the terminals, channel, and body layer. Key threats include sub-threshold leakage, gate oxide breakdown, and unauthorized signal amplification.

threats.deployment_consequence: MOSFET physical properties cannot be modified post-manufacture, making remediation through software or firmware impossible.
threats.description: An attacker might exploit sub-threshold leakage paths to infer cryptographic keys or sensitive states.
preconditions: Target is operational with cryptographic functions in use
threats.priority_rationale: Critical because leakage poses direct risks to key confidentiality without available post-deployment fixes.
threats.scenario: An attacker probes the device to measure unintended sub-threshold currents revealing cryptographic operations.
threats.sdlc_phase_description: Leakage arises from physical properties realized during the implementation phase of the MOSFET.
threats.title: Sub-threshold Leakage Exploit

threats.deployment_consequence: Requires robust oxide manufacturing; cannot be corrected post-deployment.
threats.description: Over time, or with intentional electrical stress, the gate oxide can degrade, causing uncontrolled states or failure.
threats.potential_impact: Device failure or corruption of control signals leading to denial of service or unauthorized operations.
threats.priority_rationale: High due to potential for device failure and unauthorized control. Must be addressed during manufacturing.
threats.scenario: An attacker or environmental condition induces excessive voltage across the gate oxide, leading to a breakdown.
threats.sdlc_phase_description: Manufacturing processes impact gate oxide integrity and susceptibility to breakdown.
threats.title: Gate Oxide Breakdown

threats.deployment_consequence: Design missteps allowing unauthorized amplification can only be mitigated through design changes, not patches.
threats.description: Exploitation of MOSFET characteristics to amplify signals, bypassing intended control mechanisms.
threats.potential_impact: Unauthorized activation or deactivation of circuit paths, possibly leading to functional failures or security breaches.
threats.priority_rationale: High due to impact on control integrity, though requiring direct access limits external exploit availability.
threats.scenario: Attacker interfaces physically to amplify control signals, achieving unintended operations.
threats.sdlc_phase_description: Post-deployment, physical access can enable signal manipulation that wasn't testable prior.
threats.title: Unauthorized Signal Amplification
